title: Safe Connections Act of 2022
official_summary:
Safe Connections Act of 2022

This act establishes requirements concerning access to communication services for survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking, and related harms.

At a survivor's request, a mobile service provider must separate from a shared mobile service contract the survivor's line (and the line of any individual in the survivor's care) from the abuser's line unless separation is operationally or technologically infeasible. A survivor requesting this must (1) verify through appropriate documentation that an individual under the contract committed or allegedly committed an act of domestic violence, trafficking, or a related criminal act against the survivor; and (2) assume financial responsibility for services after a line separation.

A provider may not charge fees or impose other requirements on such requests. Additionally, a provider must

  • separate the line within two business days of receiving a request;
  • allow requests to be made remotely (if feasible);
  • meet conditions related to confidentiality of, disposal of, and other matters concerning communications about requests; and
  • make information about the process for requests available through consumer-facing communications (e.g., websites).

The act (1) provides liability protection for providers' acts or omissions undertaken to comply with such requests, and (2) requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to adopt rules for these requests.

Additionally, the FCC must (1) expand access to federally subsidized communication services for survivors facing financial hardship, and (2) evaluate this expanded access.

The FCC must also consider rules requiring communication service providers to omit from consumer-facing logs calls and texts to hotlines for domestic violence and similar issues while retaining internal records.

summary.headline: This law requires mobile phone companies to separate a survivor's line from an abuser's shared plan on request, and directs the FCC to expand phone and internet subsidies for survivors.
summary.what_it_does: At a survivor's request, a mobile provider must split the survivor's line, and any line under their care, off a shared contract with the abuser, unless that is not technically possible. The survivor must provide documents showing that a person on the contract committed or allegedly committed domestic violence, trafficking, or a related crime, and must take over payments for the separated lines. Providers must complete the separation within two business days, cannot charge fees for it, and are protected from liability for good-faith compliance. The Federal Communications Commission must write rules for these requests, expand subsidized communication service for survivors facing financial hardship, and consider keeping hotline calls and texts out of consumer-facing call logs.

who_it_affects.group: Survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking, and related crimes who share a mobile phone plan with the abuser
who_it_affects.how: They can ask their mobile provider to move their line and any lines in their care onto their own account, with no fee, if they provide documentation and take over the bills.
They must separate eligible lines within two business days, make the request process available online, keep request information confidential, and follow new FCC rules.
The FCC must expand access to federally subsidized phone and internet services for them.

who_it_affects.group: People who call or text domestic violence and related hotlines
who_it_affects.how: The FCC must consider rules that would keep those contacts out of consumer-facing call and text logs while providers keep internal records.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Not stated in the summary; the FCC must first adopt implementing rules, and the exact effective dates depend on those rules.
